```sql
-- name: top_products
-- owner: merchandising
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
-- Best sellers by units and revenue. Line items reference the variant by its
-- string id (integration feed), so it is cast when joining the catalog.
WITH filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
line_agg AS (
    SELECT ol.order_id,
           pv.id         AS variant_id,
           pv.product_id,
           ol.quantity,
           ol.line_total_cents
      FROM filtered_orders fo
      JOIN order_lines ol      ON ol.order_id = fo.id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       count(DISTINCT la.order_id)     AS order_count,
       sum(la.quantity)                AS quantity,
       sum(la.line_total_cents)        AS revenue_cents,
       count(DISTINCT la.variant_id)   AS variant_count
  FROM line_agg la
  JOIN products p ON p.id = la.product_id
 GROUP BY p.id
 ORDER BY quantity DESC, revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De orders worden eerst gefilterd in een CTE, zodat de joins alleen op de relevante orderregels draaien. Het groeperen op `p.id` alleen is gelijkwaardig omdat `sku`, `name`, `brand` en `currency` functioneel afhankelijk zijn van de primary key. Bij gelijke `quantity` en `revenue_cents` blijft de volgorde van rijen niet-deterministisch, zoals in het origineel.
